2013_047_050713mtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 7, 2013, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It combines staff recognitions, April 2013 minutes, the March 2013 Treasurer's Report, bid awards tied to a proposed November 5, 2013 bond issue, and — as agenda items 8.E and 8.F — the Oakland Schools (Oakland Intermediate School District) proposed Fiscal Year 2013-2014 budget, showing total revenue of $278.8 million against total expenditures of $285.14 million. The board is asked to resolve support for that ISD budget solely to comply with Section 624 of the Revised School Code.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, May 7, 2013, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; board offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognitions and consent agenda**
Michele McKay, Senior Accounting Clerk, is named 2012-2013 Outstanding Support Staff Person of the Year, having started as a Junior Bookkeeper in April of 1979 and become Senior Bookkeeper in 1993. Roughly fifty retirees are honored, among them Mary Ellen Schultz (Barnard, 49 1/2 years) and Bob Hage (Boulan Park, 42 years). A resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 6-10, 2013. The consent agenda carries minutes of the April 9, 2013 regular meeting, the April 23, 2013 special meeting and the April 23, 2013 workshop, plus the March 2013 Treasurer's Report.

**Treasurer's Report - March 2013** (Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; memo dated April 26, 2013)

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Total check disbursements | $2,754,949.23 |
| ACH debits | $50,111.24 |
| Outgoing wire transfers | $2,868,184.77 |
| P-card purchases | $153,976.50 |
| Prior period void disbursements | ($890.00) |
| Total disbursements in period | $5,826,331.74 |

By fund: General Fund 101 $2,364,206.07; Grant Fund 120 $828.82; Special Education 122 $225,272.39; Food Service 520 $15,230.89; Troy Career Center 529 $28,787.09; Community Education 530 $15,068.56; Debt Funds 304/306/312 $22,865.67; Student Activity 700/701 $82,689.74. The summary page separately prints Total - General Fund $2,590,307.28, Total - Special Revenue Funds $59,086.54 and Total - Other Funds $105,555.41.

**Oakland Schools proposed FY 2013-2014 budget (items 8.E, 8.F)**
Presented by Mark Rajter under Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624): the ISD must submit its proposed budget to constituent boards by May 1, and each board must adopt a supporting or disapproving resolution by June 1.

| Fund | Revenue | Expenditures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All funds | $278.8 million | $285.14 million |
| General Education | $19.22M | $19.06M |
| Special Education | $129.57M | $129.43M |
| Career Focused Education | $32.1M | $32.68M |

Property tax revenue of $166.73 million supplies most ISD revenue; the deck reports annual collections down 23.1% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, an accumulative loss of $190.3 million against a FY 2008 base levy of $216.9 million and an expected FY 2014 levy of $166.7 million. PA-18 base distribution is budgeted at $110,600,000, up $1.15 million, equal to $6 per pupil in Oakland County. Total Oakland Schools bonded debt is $54,340,000 with an annual payment of $4,013,000.

**Bond issue and bids**
Dr. Fowler reports on a November 5, 2013 bond election: $125 million in three series (2014, 2017, 2020), no tax increase for residents, covering security and building modifications, technology, infrastructure, instructional equipment and 75 bus replacements. The board is asked to finalize contracts with Barton Malow for construction management (RFP 9755) and Integrated Design Solutions, LLC for information technology architect services (RFP 9756), and to award Bid 9758 for an integrated security management system to Audio Sentry Corporation in the amount of $154,855.00 from the 2012-2013 General Fund.

**Curriculum, policy and closed session**
Mathematics materials adoption for 2013-2014: Math Expressions, Common Core Edition (K-5); Big Ideas Math 2014 (6-8); Glencoe Precalculus, 2nd Edition; Big Java, 5th Edition (Cay Horsmann); A+ Computer Science Curriculum; and Calculus, 7th Edition (James Stewart). Second readings are scheduled for Board Policy G-1007 (Layoff & Recall) and G-1008 (Discipline, Demotion, or Dismissal). The meeting closes with a resolution to enter closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) for negotiations, attorney-client privilege and superintendent evaluation.

**Identification.** Board packet for the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy School District, May 7, 2013, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; board offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognitions.** Michele McKay, Senior Accounting Clerk, receives the 2012-2013 Outstanding Support Staff Award, run with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA) and Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA); she began as a Junior Bookkeeper in April of 1979 and became Senior Bookkeeper in 1993. About fifty 2012-2013 retirees are listed with service, including Mary Ellen Schultz, Barnard, 49 1/2 years; Bob Hage, Boulan Park, 42 years; Wayne Bridgland, 41 1/2 years; and Marcia Gagnon, Baker, 40 years. A resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 6-10, 2013.

**April minutes.** The April 9, 2013 meeting opened at 7:05 p.m. with Miletti absent and approximately 250 audience members, recognizing Teacher of the Year Laurie Pickell and 114 Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grants. Motion 13-027 approved consent items A-F, Yes 6, No 0; Motion 13-028 carried 6-0 for closed session at 9:05 p.m., with adjournment at 10:59 p.m. The April 23 special meeting adopted Motion 13-029 by a 6-0 roll call and adjourned Yes 7, No 0 at 7:11 p.m.

**Treasurer's Report, March 2013.** Transmitted by Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, 4400 Livernois, 248-823-4022, memo dated April 26, 2013. Disbursements by fund: General Fund (101) $2,364,206.07; Grant Fund (120) $828.82; Special Education Fund (122) $225,272.39; Food Service Fund (520) $15,230.89; Troy Career Center (529) $28,787.09; Community Education Fund (530) $15,068.56; Debt Funds (304, 306, 312) $22,865.67; Student Activity Fund (700, 701) $82,689.74; Facilities Rental (535), Building & Site (404, 499), Internal Service (681) and Memorial Scholarship (750) all zero. The summary page prints Total - General Fund $2,590,307.28, Total - Special Revenue Funds $59,086.54, Total - Other Funds $105,555.41, Total Check Disbursements $2,754,949.23, ACH Debits $50,111.24, Outgoing Wire Transfers $2,868,184.77, P-Card Purchases $153,976.50, Prior Period Void Disbursements ($890.00), and Total Disbursements in Period $5,826,331.74.

**Oakland Schools proposed FY 2013-2014 budget (item 8.E, reported by Mark Rajter).** Effective in 2004, Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624) requires each ISD to submit its budget to local districts by May 1, with local boards resolving support or disapproval by June 1. Property tax forecast against a FY 2008 base: 2008-09 -.0075%, $-; 2009-10 -3.8%, $(8.2)M; 2010-11 -11.9%, $(32.9)M; 2011-12 -7.7%, $(47.0)M; 2012-13 -2.8%, $(51.8)M; 2013-14 1%, $(50.2M); 2014-15 1%, $(48.5M); 2015-16 2%, $(45.1M); 2016-17 2%, $(41.7M); 2017-18 2%, $(38.2M). Collections declined 23.1% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, an accumulative loss of $190.3 million; the FY 2008 base year levy was $216.9 million and the FY 2014 expected levy is $166.7 million. Assumptions: property tax up 1%; interest earnings of $844K for all funds combined versus $7.7 million in FY 2007; stable General Education Section 81, Special Education and Career Focused Education state funding; no Personal Property Tax loss in FY14. The Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve was doubled in 2011-12 from 1.5% to 3%, sits at 2.5% for 2012-13 equating to $3.2 million in expense, is projected at 1.25% for 2013-14, with $10.2 million paid to date; PA 18 special education funding rises $1.15 million, an increase of $6 per pupil in Oakland County.

Total FY 2014 revenue is $278.8 million: property tax $166.73M, state $6.69M, other local $19.09M, other financing sources $11.82M, new grant award funding $60.8M, estimated grant carryover $13.67M (pie percentages printed are 4%, 19%, 8%, 63%, 2%, 7%, with 63% belonging to property tax). Total FY 2014 expenditures are $285.14 million: transfers to LEAs/other funds $131.6M (46.2%), personnel $51.13M (17.9%), purchased services, supplies, dues and fees $19.83M (7.0%), utilities $.89M (0.3%), grant related expenditures $74.47M (26.1%), capital outlay and other $3.22M (1.1%), debt service $4.0M (1.4%).

General Education Fund revenue is $19.22M (property tax $9.91M, 51.5%; other local $4.52M; state $3.52M; other financing $1.27M) against expenditures of $19.06M (general administration $1.65M, finance and operations $6.79M, instructional services $9.96M, plant and fixed charges plus LEA transfers $.66M). Its five-year forecast in millions runs revenue 19.22, 18.62, 18.85, 18.9, 19.1 against expenditures 19.06, 19.06, 19.11, 19.03, 19.16, with operating results of .16, (.44), (.26), (.09), (.005), end-of-year fund balances of 2.24, 1.84, 1.53, 1.21, .91 and unreserved fund balance percentages of 8.18%, 6.17%, 4.95%, 4.57%, 4.52%.

Special Education Fund revenue is $129.57M (property tax $125.96M, 97.2%; other local $.75M; state $2.6M; other financing $0.26M) against expenditures of $129.43M (program supervision and direction $2.27M, program operations $7.29M, plant and fixed charges $6.67M, LEA transfers and program subsidies $113.2M). FY 2014 special education support and subsidies: PA-18 base distribution $110,600,000; Section 24 subsidy/other $175,000; group homes $1,600,000; Havenwick $150,000; SEI Regional Day Treatment $450,000; total $112,975,000. The five-year forecast in millions shows revenue 129.57, 131.16, 133.72, 136.34, 139.0 against expenditures 129.43, 130.94, 133.57, 136.12, 138.78, operating excess of .140, .226, .159, .216, .216, restricted center program facility renovation balances of 1.146, 1.356, 1.566, 1.776, 1.986, restricted special education balances of .822, .839, .789, .795, .801, totals of 1.969, 2.195, 2.355, 2.571, 2.787, and restricted fund balance net of LEA operating transfer at 5.00% every year.

Career Focused Education Fund revenue is $32.1M (property tax $30.85M, 96.1%; other local $0.44M; state $0.57M; other financing $0.24M) against expenditures of $32.68M (campus and other program administration $20.6M, LEA transfers and direct program operations $4.76M, plant and fixed charges $7.32M). Its forecast in millions shows revenue 31.11, 32.50, 33.13, 33.77, 34.43 against expenditures 32.68, 33.24, 33.75, 34.14, 34.44, deficits of (.570), (.736), (.622), (.372), (.001), restricted balances of 3.5, 2.7, 2.1, 1.7, 1.7 and percentages of 10.8%, 8.4%, 6.43%, 5.27%, 5.18%. Grants and funded projects total $74.4M — new awards $60.8M and carryover $13.6M — with $62.8M transferred directly to districts and $11.2M administered by the ISD including JobLink at $5.2M. FY 2014 district debt: CFEF principal $41,870,000 with a $3,088,000 annual payment; QSCB principal $14,800,000 with a $925,000 annual payment; total bonded debt $54,340,000 and $4,013,000 annually. The QSCB issue is pre-funded in Debt Service Fund 314 and the 2007 campus renovations bond in Debt Service Fund 312 through FY 2022.

**Item 8.F.** The Troy Board of Education resolves that it has reviewed the proposed ISD budget and expresses support, adding that Troy's support is "for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624"; the resolution goes to the intermediate school board no later than June 1, 2013.

**Bond report (8.A).** Dr. Fowler reports a November 5, 2013 election, the last bond issue having been in 2004. Categories are security and building modifications, technology, infrastructure, instructional equipment and transportation, citing a 9-year bus lifespan, 75 total bus replacements and 7,000+ students transported daily. The scope is three series in 2014, 2017 and 2020 totaling $125 million with no tax increase; the breakdown pie prints 6%, 5%, 22%, 55% and 12%.

**Bids (8.B, 8.C, 8.D).** RFP 9755, Construction Management Services: 8 bidders invited, 5 responding, 4 interviewed; bidding opened March 20, 2013 and closed April 3, 2013; the committee of Dr. Barbara Fowler, Mark Rajter, Kenneth Miller and Todd Hensley (memo April 18, 2013, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083) recommends Barton Malow at a 1.85% professional fee, 2.5 to 3.4% management fee and 1.5 to 2.0% general conditions, with technology design a voluntary alternate at an additional 2.5%; George W. Auch Company, Clark Construction Company, McCarthy & Smith, Inc. and Skanska USA Building Inc. also bid. RFP 9756, Information Technology Architect Services: 8 invited, 7 responding (two unsolicited), 3 interviewed; Integrated Design Solutions, LLC recommended at a flat 4.54%, against Barton Malow at 4.75-5.85%, Fanning/Howey Associates, Plante & Moran PLLC, Secant Technologies and SHW Group LLC. Bid 9758, Integrated Security Management System (memo 30 April 2013, Kenneth D. Miller): Audio Sentry Corporation $154,855.00, Mechanical Controls & Maintenance, Inc. $197,166.00 (Andover Controls alternate), Midstate Security Company, LLC $209,634.00, charged to the 2012-2013 General Fund.

**Curriculum and superintendent goals.** On Kris Karbon's April 9, 2013 recommendation, the board is asked to approve for 2013-2014: Math Expressions, Common Core Edition (K-5); Big Ideas Math 2014 (6-8); Precalculus, 2nd Edition by Glencoe; Big Java, 5th Edition by Cay Horsmann; the A+ Computer Science Curriculum; and Calculus, 7th Edition by James Stewart. Superintendent goals report 100% of 4th grade teachers participating in teacher lab three times, over 24 teachers trained in MI CLASS literacy in grades 6-12, a middle school math support class adding 3 hours of instruction per week, a TMP Architecture facility assessment, and a Department of Treasury bond application review June 10-26, 2013. Troy will move from a Finance/Human Resources system costing $12+ per student to Oakland Schools' Tyler Munis with 22 other districts over four fiscal years, subsidized for five years and roughly $10 per student thereafter.

**Policies and closed session.** Board Policy G-1007, Layoff and Recall of Teachers and Administrators, receives second reading and adoption: decisions must be based on retaining effective teachers and administrators, may not use length of service or tenure status as primary or determining factors, and may not be subject to collective bargaining; sources are Section 380.1248 of the Revised School Code and Section 423.215(3)(k). Board Policy G-1008 applies the Michigan Teachers' Tenure Act, MCL 38.71 through 38.191, permitting discipline, demotion or dismissal only for a reason that is not arbitrary or capricious under MCL 38.101; sources are MCL 38.71-191 and MCL 423.215(3)(m). Item 11.A resolves, under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to enter closed session on negotiations, attorney-client privilege and superintendent evaluation, roll call Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds and Fleming.
